definitions.gloss: tenant; shop or business renting space in a building
definitions.explanation: A shop, restaurant, or business that rents space within a larger building such as a department store, shopping mall, or office building. From English 'tenant.' In Japanese, this word emphasizes the commercial tenant rather than residential renters.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧テナント⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{十|じゅう}→十：00708_juu⟧⟦{店舗|てんぽ}→店舗：12481_tenpo⟧⟦{入|はい}っている→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: This building has ten tenant shops.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一階|いっかい}→一階：27512_ikkai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧テナント⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{撤退|てったい}した→撤退する：25360_tettaisuru⟧。
examples.english: The first-floor tenant has moved out.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧テナント⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{募集|ぼしゅう}→募集：03035_boshuu⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦カフェ→カフェ：06767_kafe⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}こう→開く：01979_hiraku⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{考|かんが}えている→考える：00856_kangaeru⟧。
examples.english: They're looking for tenants in the building in front of the station, so I'm thinking of opening a café.

notes:
From English 'tenant,' but in Japanese the word primarily refers to commercial tenants — shops and businesses that rent space in a larger building. Residential renters are typically called {借|か}り{主|ぬし} or ⟦{入居者|にゅうきょしゃ}→入居者：20979_nyuukyosha⟧, not テナント.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- テナント⟦{募集|ぼしゅう}→募集：03035_boshuu⟧: tenant wanted; space for rent
- テナント⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧: a tenant moves in
- テナント⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{撤退|てったい}する→撤退する：25360_tettaisuru⟧: a tenant moves out
- テナント⟦{料|りょう}→料：28172_ryou⟧: tenant fee; rent
- テナントビル: tenant building (multi-tenant commercial building)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {借|か}り{主|ぬし}: renter; lessee — used for residential renters
- ⟦{入居者|にゅうきょしゃ}→入居者：20979_nyuukyosha⟧: occupant; resident — broader term for anyone occupying a space
- {店子|たなこ}: tenant (traditional) — older Japanese word for a renter, now less common
